Below is a taxonomy built only from the rules you provided. I group the puzzles by the main thing the solver is asked to construct on the grid.

---

# Taxonomy of the listed grid-based logic games

## I. Loop-drawing puzzles
Goal: draw one closed loop, usually non-branching and non-self-crossing.

### A. Cell-center loop puzzles
The loop passes through centers of cells.

- **Dotchi-Loop**  
  Single loop through cells; must pass white circles, avoid black circles; white circles in a room are all straight or all turning.

- **Masyu**  
  Single loop through all black and white circles; white circles force straight passage, black circles force turns with straight continuation.

- **Mid-loop**  
  Single loop through cells; each black circle is the midpoint of a straight segment of the loop.

- **Moon-or-Sun**  
  Single loop; each room is entered once; in each room the loop uses either all moons or all suns, alternating by room.

- **Nagareru**  
  Single directed loop; must pass arrow cells; wind directions constrain movement and turning.

- **Suraromu**  
  Single loop through cells; must pass all gates exactly once each; numbered gates constrain crossing order from the start cell.

- **Yajilin**  
  Single loop through cells; numbered arrow cells count black cells in the arrow direction; loop avoids black and clue cells.

### B. Dot-edge loop puzzles
The loop is drawn by connecting adjacent dots.

- **Slitherlink**  
  Single loop on the dot lattice; numbers give how many surrounding edges are used.

---

## II. Path-connection puzzles
Goal: connect endpoints or route paths, but not necessarily as a single loop.

### A. Pair-connection paths
- **Numberlink**  
  Connect pairs of equal numbers with non-crossing, non-branching paths through cells.

### B. Directed or emitted paths from marked objects
- **Pencils**  
  Mark straight pencils with a tip at one end; draw a line from each tip; numbers indicate pencil length and line length.

### C. Movement-to-destination puzzles
- **Satogaeri**  
  Move circles orthogonally so each country ends with one circle; numbered circles move exactly that many cells; paths cannot cross or pass over circles.

- **Yosenabe**  
  Move circles orthogonally into gray areas using straight arrows; arrows do not bend or cross; gray-area numbers equal sums of entering circles.

---

## III. Region-division puzzles
Goal: partition the grid into blocks/regions by drawing borders or determining region membership.

### A. Divide into size-constrained regions
- **Five Cells**  
  Divide grid into blocks of exactly five cells; numbers count surrounding block edges.

- **Shikaku**  
  Divide grid into rectangles; each rectangle contains one number equal to its area.

### B. Divide into shape-constrained regions
- **Sashigane**  
  Divide grid into one-cell-wide L-shaped blocks; circles mark knees, arrows mark ends, numbers give block size.

- **Double Choco**  
  Divide grid into blocks; each block contains matching white and gray areas of the same shape.

---

## IV. Area-filling / shading puzzles
Goal: color cells black/white or shaded/unshaded under structural constraints.

### A. Black/white shading with connectivity constraints
- **Heyawake**  
  Shade cells by room counts; black cells cannot touch; white cells connected; white runs cannot cross more than two rooms in a line.

- **Hitori**  
  Shade cells so row/column numbers are unique among white cells; black cells cannot touch; white cells connected.

- **Kurodoko**  
  Shade black cells; numbered white cells count visible white cells; black cells cannot touch; white cells connected.

- **Nurikabe**  
  Fill cells black/white; numbered white islands have given sizes; black cells form one connected wall; no 2×2 black block.

- **Usowan**  
  Shade cells; numbers count adjacent shaded cells except one wrong clue per room; shaded cells cannot touch; white cells connected.

### B. Shading with room-based quotas or paired-block conditions
- **Norinori**  
  Shade cells in dominoes of two consecutive black squares; each room contains exactly two black squares.

- **Nuritwin**  
  Each region contains exactly two shaded blocks of equal size; all shaded cells globally connected; same-region blocks do not touch; no 2×2 shaded block.

- **Sto-stone**  
  Shade cells in rooms according to counts of continuous black cells; black cells cannot connect across room borders; after “dropping,” stones fill the bottom half.

### C. Shading with local clue counts or ray sums
- **Akari**  
  Place bulbs in white cells; numbered black cells count adjacent bulbs; bulbs illuminate orthogonally; all white cells lit; bulbs cannot see each other.

- **Kurotto**  
  Shade cells black; circle numbers give the sum of continuous black-cell runs extending orthogonally from the circle; circle cells stay unshaded.

### D. Shading with shape restrictions on connected components
- **Choco Banana**  
  Black connected components must be rectangles/squares; white connected components must not be rectangles/squares; numbers give area size.

- **Shakashaka**  
  Place triangular black halves in cells; remaining white parts must form rectangles/squares; numbered black cells count adjacent triangles.

- **Tilepaint**  
  Color whole tiles black or white; diagonal clues count black cells to the right/down until another clue or border; final picture forms an outline.

### E. Shading with promontory / endpoint structure
- **Nurimisaki**  
  Circled cells are white “misaki” cells with exactly one white orthogonal neighbor; numbers give straight-line white length; white connected; no 2×2 black or white block.

### F. Shading with tetromino or polyform placement
- **LITS**  
  Shade a tetromino in each room; same tetromino shape cannot touch across rooms; shaded cells connected; no 2×2 shaded square.

### G. Room-wise all-or-nothing shading
- **Nurimeizu**  
  Entire rooms are either all black or all white; create a maze from S to G through white cells; circles lie on shortest path, triangles do not; no 2×2 monochrome block.

---

## V. Number-placement puzzles
Goal: fill cells with numbers under arithmetic, adjacency, or region rules.

### A. Latin / permutation-style placement
- **Sudoku**  
  Fill 1–9 so each row, column, and 3×3 box contains all digits 1–9.

- **Makaro**  
  Each room contains numbers 1 up to room size; arrow clues indicate the largest adjacent number; equal numbers cannot touch across rooms.

### B. Region-size-equals-number puzzles
- **Fillomino**  
  Partition into same-number regions; each region’s size equals its number; equal-sized regions cannot touch orthogonally.

### C. Distance-separation number placement
- **Ripple Effect**  
  Each room contains consecutive numbers from 1; equal numbers in a row/column must be separated by at least their value.

### D. Number fitting from a given list
- **Nansuke**  
  Fill blank cells with numbers from a provided list; entries run horizontally or vertically.

---

## VI. Symbol-placement puzzles
Goal: fill cells with non-numeric symbols under run or territory constraints.

- **Juosan**  
  Fill each cell with — or |; territory clues compare counts of the two symbols; horizontal and vertical run-length restrictions differ by symbol.

---

## VII. Object-placement / polyform-growth puzzles
Goal: place discrete objects or marked cells that form blocks with growth or uniqueness rules.

### A. Growth-sequence block puzzles
- **Evolomino**  
  Place squares in cells; each connected block contains exactly one square on a pre-drawn arrow; along an arrow, later blocks are formed by adding one square without rotation/flipping.

### B. Block-identification by black-cell components
- **Chained Block**  
  Fill cells black/white; each black connected component is a block whose size is given by its clue or ?; every block belongs to a corner-touching chain; no chain may contain duplicate size-and-shape blocks up to rotation/reflection.

---

## VIII. Network-construction puzzles
Goal: build a connected graph-like structure rather than a path through cells.

- **Hashiwokakero**  
  Connect numbered islands with 1 or 2 bridges; bridges cannot cross islands or bridges; all islands become one connected network.

---

## IX. Sequence / creature-placement puzzles
Goal: place ordered sequences in cells with visibility or contact constraints.

- **Hebi**  
  Place snake numbers 1 to 5 in white cells as consecutive chains; snakes cannot touch; snakes cannot appear in another snake’s forward line of sight; arrow clues in black cells indicate nearest seen snake number or 0.

---

# Cross-cutting secondary taxonomy

Some puzzles fit multiple structural ideas. Using only the rules, they can also be classified by secondary features.

## A. Uses bold-lined rooms/areas
- Dotchi-Loop
- Double Choco
- Heyawake
- Juosan
- LITS
- Moon-or-Sun
- Nurimeizu
- Nuritwin
- Ripple Effect
- Sto-stone
- Tilepaint
- Usowan
- Makaro
- Norinori
- Satogaeri

## B. Requires global connectivity of shaded/white/network structure
- Hashiwokakero — all islands connected
- Heyawake — white cells connected
- Hitori — white cells connected
- Kurodoko — white cells connected
- LITS — shaded cells connected
- Nurikabe — black cells connected
- Nurimisaki — white cells connected
- Nuritwin — shaded cells connected
- Usowan — white cells connected

## C. Forbids 2×2 monochrome/shaded blocks
- LITS — no 2×2 shaded square
- Nurikabe — no 2×2 black block
- Nurimeizu — neither black nor white may form 2×2 or larger squares
- Nurimisaki — neither black nor white may form 2×2 or larger squares
- Nuritwin — no 2×2 shaded block

## D. Uses visibility / line-of-sight clues
- Akari — bulb illumination along row/column
- Hebi — snake line of sight
- Kurodoko — visible white-cell count to nearest black or border
- Kurotto — continuous black-cell runs from circles
- Tilepaint — counts black cells rightward/downward
- Yajilin — counts black cells in arrow direction

## E. Uses shape equivalence up to rotation/reflection
- Chained Block
- Double Choco
- LITS
- Evolomino (explicitly forbids rotation/flipping in growth)
- Nuritwin (equal size only, not explicitly same shape, so not included)

## F. Uses movement rather than static placement
- Satogaeri
- Yosenabe

---
